literal: " He thereupon seized and executed Opening-Fu Yitong Third Rank Chilie Yanqing, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xin Xiong, Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Xiaofen, Minister of Justice Liu Yin, Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Ji, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Shibi — punishing their disloyalty.
idiomatic: He then arrested and executed Chilie Yanqing, Xin Xiong, Cui Xiaofen, Liu Yin, Yang Ji, and Yuan Shibi—punishing their treason.

literal: Shibi's household was confiscated.
idiomatic: Yuan Shibi's household was confiscated.

literal: Shenwu, because myriad affairs could not be neglected, consulted the hundred officials and made Prince of Qinghe Yuan Dan Grand Marshal, dwelling in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing to receive orders and decide affairs.
idiomatic: State business could not stand idle; Gao Huan consulted the officials and made Prince of Qinghe Yuan Dan Grand Marshal, lodging in the ministers' lower quarters to receive orders and govern.

literal: The prince used the language of imperial guard and escort; Shenwu found it ugly.
idiomatic: The prince spoke as though already an emperor on procession; Gao Huan took offense.

literal: Shenwu soon reached Hengnong, then west seized Tong Pass and captured Mao Hongbin.
idiomatic: Gao Huan soon reached Hengnong, stormed Tong Pass to the west, and captured Mao Hongbin.

literal: Advancing to Changcheng, Longmen Inspector Xue Chongli surrendered.
idiomatic: As he advanced on Changcheng, Longmen Inspector Xue Chongli surrendered.

literal: Shenwu withdrew and encamped at Hedong, ordering Mobile Court Chief Secretary Xue Yu to hold Tong Pass and Grand Commander Kudi Wen to hold Fengling.
idiomatic: Gao Huan withdrew to Hedong and ordered Xue Yu to hold Tong Pass and Kudi Wen to hold Fengling.

literal: He built a fortress on the west bank of Pujin, held Hua Province, made Xue Shaozong governor, and Gao Ao handled Yuzhou affairs.
idiomatic: On the west bank of Pujin he built a fortress and held Hua Province, appointing Xue Shaozong governor and putting Gao Ao in charge of Yuzhou.

literal: From departing Jinyang to this point Shenwu had sent forty memorials in all; the Wei Emperor answered none.
idiomatic: From the day he left Jinyang, Gao Huan had sent forty memorials; the Wei Emperor answered not one.

literal: On the gengyin day of the ninth month Shenwu returned to Luoyang and sent the monk Daorong to present a memorial to Guanzhong; again no answer.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the ninth month Gao Huan returned to Luoyang and sent the monk Daorong with a memorial to Guanzhong; again there was no reply.

literal: He then gathered the hundred officials and elders of the Four Gates to discuss whom to install.
idiomatic: He gathered officials and elders at the Four Gates to decide whom to enthrone.

literal: They held that since the Xiaochang turmoil the dynastic line had been severed, spirit tablets had none to rely on, and zhao and mu were out of order.
idiomatic: They held that since the Xiaochang upheaval the imperial line had broken, the ancestral tablets stood orphaned, and the order of the temple was lost.

literal: Yongan took Emperor Xiaowen as uncle-ancestor; Yongxi moved Emperor Xiaoming to a side-chamber — the realm lost its mandate and reigns were brief for this reason.
idiomatic: Under Yongan, Emperor Xiaowen was made a collateral ancestor; under Yongxi, Emperor Xiaoming was moved to a side chamber—the realm lost its mandate and reigns were cut short for this reason.

literal: They thereupon resolved to install Prince of Qinghe's heir Shan Jian.
idiomatic: They resolved to install Shan Jian, heir of the Prince of Qinghe.

literal: Once the decision was settled, they informed Prince of Qinghe.
idiomatic: When the choice was settled they informed the Prince of Qinghe.

literal: The prince said: "An emperor has no father; if my son is to be installed, I hold my remaining years cheap.
idiomatic: The prince said, "An emperor has no father; if my son is to reign, I count the rest of my life as nothing.

literal: " He was thereupon installed — this is Emperor Xiaojing.
idiomatic: The boy was enthroned as Emperor Xiaojing.

literal: Wei was thus first divided into two.
idiomatic: Wei was thus split in two.

literal: Shenwu, because Emperor Xiaowu had already gone west, feared pressure on the Xiao and Shan passes; Luoyang again lay south of the river and close to Liang territory — if he turned toward Jinyang the terrain could not connect; he therefore proposed moving the capital to Ye, and Protector of the Army Zu Ying approved.
idiomatic: With Emperor Xiaowu gone west, Gao Huan feared pressure on the Xiao and Shan passes; Luoyang lay south of the river and hard against Liang territory, and the route to Jinyang could not be held together—he proposed moving the capital to Ye, and Zu Ying approved.

literal: Three days after the edict was issued the imperial carriage set out; four hundred thousand households fled the road in disorder.
idiomatic: Three days after the edict the court set out; four hundred thousand households stumbled onto the road in disorder.

literal: Shenwu remained in Luoyang to settle affairs, then returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Gao Huan stayed in Luoyang to settle affairs, then returned to Jinyang.

literal: From this time military and state affairs all devolved on the chancellor's office.
idiomatic: From then on military and civil affairs all passed to the chancellor's office.

literal: Earlier a children's song ran: "Pity the green sparrow fledgling, flying into Ye city; wings nearly formed, it turns into a parrot fledgling.
idiomatic: A children's song had run, "Pity the green sparrow fledgling, flying into Ye; wings nearly grown, it turns into a parrot fledgling.

literal: " Those who delighted in such things whispered that the sparrow meant the Wei Emperor, son of Prince of Qinghe, and the parrot meant Shenwu.
idiomatic: Gossip said the sparrow meant the Qinghe prince who became emperor, and the parrot meant Gao Huan.

literal: Initially, in Xiaochang times, Mountain Hu Liu Lish sheng declared himself Son of Heaven, era name Shenjia, dwelling at Yunyang Valley; the western lands were raided by him year after year — they called it the Hu wilderness.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang times the Mountain Hu leader Liu Lish sheng had declared himself emperor under the era Shenjia and dwelt at Yunyang Valley; the west was raided year after year—men called it the Hu wilderness.

literal: In the first month of the second year, Western Wei Weizhou Governor Kezhuhun Daoyuan brought his followers over in submission; Shenwu received and enrolled them.
idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Western Wei Governor of Weizhou Kezhuhun Daoyuan brought his followers over; Gao Huan received them.

literal: On the renxu day Shenwu attacked Liu Lish sheng by surprise and routed him greatly.
idiomatic: On the renxu day Gao Huan struck Liu Lish sheng by surprise and routed him.

literal: On the jisi day the Wei Emperor issued an edict of praise, making Shenwu Chancellor, granting the yellow axe, sword in court, shoes on the hall floor, and no hurrying in audience.
idiomatic: On the jisi day the Wei Emperor issued a commendatory edict making Gao Huan Chancellor, granting the yellow battle-axe, permission to wear sword and shoes in court, and exemption from hurrying in audience.

literal: Shenwu firmly declined.
idiomatic: Gao Huan firmly declined.

literal: In the third month Shenwu wished to marry his daughter to Lish sheng's heir; waiting until they were off guard, on the xinyou day he struck with a hidden force.
idiomatic: In the third month Gao Huan offered his daughter to Lish sheng's heir; when their guard was down, on the xinyou day he struck with a hidden force.

literal: The northern king beheaded Lish sheng and sent the head.
idiomatic: The northern king beheaded Lish sheng and sent his head.

literal: His followers again installed his son Nanhai Wang; Shenwu advanced to attack and again captured Nanhai Wang, his brothers Xihai Wang and Beihai Wang, the empress, more than four hundred officials and below, and fifty thousand Hu and Wei households.
idiomatic: His followers installed his son as Nanhai Wang; Gao Huan pressed the attack and captured Nanhai Wang, his brothers Xihai Wang and Beihai Wang, the empress, more than four hundred officials, and fifty thousand Hu and Wei households.

literal: On the renshen day Shenwu attended court at Ye.
idiomatic: On the renshen day Gao Huan attended court at Ye.

literal: In the fourth month Shenwu asked to provide grain rations to relocated people in varying amounts.
idiomatic: In the fourth month Gao Huan asked that relocated people be given grain rations according to rank.

literal: On the jiayin day of the ninth month Shenwu, because prefectural, commandery, and county officials widely violated the law, asked to send envoys to inquire into the people's hardships.
idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the ninth month Gao Huan, citing widespread maladministration in the provinces, asked to send envoys to inquire into the people's hardships.

literal: On the jiazi day of the first month of the third year Shenwu led ten thousand horse under Kudi Gan and others to raid Western Wei Xia Province; he ate nothing cooked and arrived in four days.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the first month of the third year Gao Huan led ten thousand horsemen under Kudi Gan against Western Wei Xia Province, eating nothing cooked, and arrived in four days.

literal: Binding spears into ladders, by night they entered the city, captured Governor Feiye Tou Hubo E-mitu, and thereupon employed him.
idiomatic: They bound spears into ladders, entered the city by night, seized Governor Hubo E-mitu of the Feiye Tou tribe, and put him to use.

literal: He left Commander Zhang Qiong to garrison and defend, and moved five thousand households of the tribe back.
idiomatic: He left Zhang Qiong to garrison the place and moved five thousand tribal households back with him.

literal: Western Wei Lingzhou Governor Cao Ni and his son-in-law Liangzhou Governor Liu Feng sent envoys requesting to come over in submission.
idiomatic: Western Wei Governor of Lingzhou Cao Ni and his son-in-law, Governor of Liangzhou Liu Feng, sent envoys offering submission.

literal: Yuwen Tai besieged Ni and flooded the city with water; four feet remained above the water.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai besieged Cao Ni and flooded the city until only four feet of wall stood above the water.

literal: Shenwu ordered Azoluo to dispatch thirty thousand cavalry to cross straight through Ling Province, circle behind the Western army, capture fifty horses, and the Western force thereupon withdrew.
idiomatic: Gao Huan ordered the Azoluo to send thirty thousand cavalry through Ling Province, swing behind the Western army, seize fifty horses, and the Western force withdrew.

literal: Shenwu led cavalry to welcome Ni and Feng; he brought back five thousand surviving households and restored Ni's office and rank.
idiomatic: Gao Huan rode out to welcome Cao Ni and Liu Feng, brought back five thousand surviving households, and restored Cao Ni's office and rank.

literal: The Wei Emperor issued an edict adding the Nine Bestowments to Shenwu; he firmly declined and it stopped.
idiomatic: The Wei Emperor offered Gao Huan the Nine Bestowments; he declined firmly and the matter ended.

literal: In the second month Shenwu ordered Azoluo to press Western Wei Qinzhou Governor Prince of Jianzhong Wan Shi Pu-ba; Shenwu marched with his host in response.
idiomatic: In the second month Gao Huan ordered the Azoluo to press Western Wei Governor of Qinzhou Wan Shi Pu-ba, Prince of Jianzhong, and marched with his main force in support.

literal: On the jiawu day of the sixth month Pu-ba, his son Taizai Shouluogan, Binzhou Governor Chigan Baole, Right Guard General Poliuhan Chang, and more than three hundred commanders and generals came over with their followers.
idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the sixth month Pu-ba, his son Shouluogan, Binzhou Governor Chigan Baole, Right Guard General Poliuhan Chang, and more than three hundred officers came over with their followers.

literal: On the dinghai day of the eighth month Shenwu asked to standardize the bushel measure and distribute it throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the eighth month Gao Huan asked to standardize the bushel measure and issue it throughout the realm.

literal: On the xinhai day of the ninth month Fenzhou Hu kings Tiaochu and Cao Erlong gathered followers in rebellion, set up officials, and era name Pingdu.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the ninth month the Fenzhou Hu leaders Tiaochu and Cao Erlong rebelled, set up a court, and declared the era Pingdu.

literal: Shenwu suppressed and pacified them.
idiomatic: Gao Huan suppressed and pacified them.

literal: On the dingchou day of the twelfth month Shenwu marched west from Jinyang to campaign, sending Vice Minister Mobile Court Prince of Ruyang Xian and Minister of Works Gao Ao toward Shangluo, and Grand Commander Dou Tai in through Tong Pass.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the twelfth month Gao Huan marched west from Jinyang, sending Prince of Ruyang Xian and Gao Ao toward Shangluo and Grand Commander Dou Tai in through Tong Pass.

literal: On the guichou day of the first month of the fourth year Dou Tai's army was defeated and he killed himself.
idiomatic: On the guichou day of the first month of the fourth year Dou Tai's army was broken and he killed himself.

literal: Shenwu halted at Pujin; because the ice was thin he could not cross to the rescue, and thereupon withdrew the army.
idiomatic: Gao Huan halted at Pujin; the ice was too thin to cross to the rescue, and he withdrew.

literal: Gao Ao attacked and captured Shangluo.
idiomatic: Gao Ao stormed and took Shangluo.

literal: On the yiyou day of the second month Shenwu, because Bing, Si, Fen, Jian, Jin, East Yong, South Fen, Tai, and Shan — nine provinces — had suffered frost and drought and people were starving and scattering, asked that granaries everywhere be opened for relief.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the second month Gao Huan, citing frost and drought in nine provinces—Bing, Si, Fen, Jian, Jin, East Yong, South Fen, Tai, and Shan—and famine and flight among the people, asked that granaries be opened for relief.

literal: On the renshen day of the sixth month Shenwu went to Tianchi, obtained an auspicious stone with raised characters reading "Six Kings Three Rivers."
idiomatic: On the renshen day of the sixth month Gao Huan visited Tianchi and found an auspicious stone bearing raised characters: "Six Kings Three Rivers."

literal: On the renchen day of the tenth month Shenwu marched west to campaign, crossing from Pujin with two hundred thousand men.
idiomatic: On the renchen day of the tenth month Gao Huan marched west, crossing at Pujin with two hundred thousand men.

literal: Yuwen Tai encamped at Shawei.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai drew up his army at Shawei.

literal: Shenwu, because the ground was narrow and obstructed, withdrew slightly; the Western men shouted and advanced; the army fell into great disorder and abandoned one hundred eighty thousand pieces of arms and armor; Shenwu crossed on a camel and waited for a boat to return.
idiomatic: On cramped ground Gao Huan drew back slightly; the Western troops shouted and charged; his army broke in chaos and cast away one hundred eighty thousand sets of arms and armor; Gao Huan crossed on a camel and waited for a boat to escape.

literal: In the third month of the first year of Yuanxiang, on the xinyou day, Shenwu firmly asked to resign the chancellorship; the Wei Emperor permitted it.
idiomatic: In the third month of Yuanxiang 1 (539), on the xinyou day, Gao Huan firmly asked to resign the chancellorship; the Wei Emperor agreed.

literal: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Shenwu attended court at Ye; on the renchen day he returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Gao Huan attended court at Ye; on the renchen day he returned to Jinyang.

literal: He asked to lift the prohibition on wine and also to give relief to palace guard military officers.
idiomatic: He asked to lift the ban on wine and to grant relief to the palace guard officers.

literal: On the renwu day of the seventh month Mobile Court Hou Jing and Minister of Works Gao Ao besieged Western Wei General Dugu Xin at Jinyong; the Western Wei Emperor and Yuwen Tai both came to the rescue.
idiomatic: On the renwu day of the seventh month Hou Jing and Gao Ao besieged Western Wei General Dugu Xin at Jinyong; the Western Wei Emperor and Yuwen Tai both marched to relieve him.

literal: Grand Commander Kudi Gan led the generals as vanguard; Shenwu commanded the host and followed.
idiomatic: Grand Commander Kudi Gan led the vanguard; Gao Huan followed with the main army.

literal: On the xinmao day of the eighth month they fought at Heyin and routed the Western Wei army greatly, capturing tens of thousands.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the eighth month they fought at Heyin and broke the Western Wei army, taking tens of thousands captive.

literal: Minister of Works Gao Ao, Grand Commander Li Meng, and Song Xian died in the action.
idiomatic: Gao Ao, Li Meng, and Song Xian were killed.

literal: In the Western army's defeat Dugu Xin entered the pass first; Yuwen Tai left his commander Sun Ziyan to hold Jinyong and thereupon burned the camp and fled.
idiomatic: In the rout Dugu Xin fled into the pass first; Yuwen Tai left Sun Ziyan to hold Jinyong, burned the camp, and escaped.

literal: Shenwu sent troops in pursuit to Xiao, could not overtake them, and returned.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sent pursuit as far as Xiao, failed to overtake them, and turned back.

literal: Initially, when Shenwu learned the Western army was coming to invade, he led his host in haste from Jinyang; reaching Mengjin, before he had crossed, the battle already had its outcome.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan learned the Western army was advancing, he rushed from Jinyang to Mengjin; before he crossed the river the battle was already decided.

literal: Presently Shenwu crossed the river; Sun Ziyan also abandoned the city and fled; Shenwu thereupon destroyed Jinyong and returned.
idiomatic: Gao Huan crossed the river; Sun Ziyan abandoned the city and fled; Gao Huan demolished Jinyong and returned.

literal: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month Shenwu attended court at the capital.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month Gao Huan attended court at the capital.

literal: On the renchen day of the twelfth month he returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the renchen day of the twelfth month he returned to Jinyang.

literal: On the dingchou day of the seventh month of the first year of Xinghe the Wei Emperor promoted Shenwu to Chancellor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he firmly declined and it stopped.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the seventh month of Xinghe 1 (539), the Wei Emperor promoted Gao Huan to Chancellor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he declined firmly and the matter ended.

literal: On the yichou day of the eleventh month Shenwu, because the new palace was complete, attended court at Ye.
idiomatic: On the yichou day of the eleventh month, with the new palace complete, Gao Huan attended court at Ye.

literal: The Wei Emperor feasted and shot arrows with Shenwu; Shenwu descended the steps to offer congratulations, and again declined Prince of Bohai and Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without; an edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: The Wei Emperor feasted and shot arrows with Gao Huan; Gao Huan came down the steps to congratulate him and again declined the title Prince of Bohai and command of all armies—the edict would not allow it.

literal: On the wuxu day of the twelfth month Shenwu returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the twelfth month Gao Huan returned to Jinyang.

literal: In the twelfth month of the second year a branch of the Azoluo sent envoys requesting surrender.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year a branch of the Azoluo sent envoys offering surrender.

literal: Shenwu led his host to welcome them; going out through Wuzhou Pass he saw no one, hunted greatly, and returned.
idiomatic: Gao Huan marched out to welcome them; beyond Wuzhou Pass he found no one, hunted at length, and returned.

literal: In the fifth month of the third year Shenwu toured the northern frontier and sent envoys to make peace with the Rouran.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year Gao Huan toured the northern frontier and sent envoys to treat with the Rouran.

literal: On the xinsi day of the fifth month of the fourth year Shenwu attended court at Ye and asked that the hundred officials each month present affairs face to face, that worthies in humble places be brought forward, that remonstrance be received and evil turned aside, that lawsuits be judged in person, and that diligence and slackness be rewarded and punished;
idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the fifth month of the fourth year Gao Huan attended court at Ye and asked that officials each month report affairs in person, that hidden talent be brought forward, that remonstrance be welcomed and corruption driven out, that he judge lawsuits himself, and that diligence and neglect be rewarded and punished;

literal: where prefects and governors were at fault, punishment should descend by rank;
idiomatic: that governors and prefects who erred should be punished by descending ranks;

literal: within the inner quarters, access to the emperor should follow proper order;
idiomatic: that within the inner palace imperial access should follow proper order;

literal: hawks and hounds of the rear garden should all be cast away.
idiomatic: and that the hawks and hounds of the rear garden should all be abandoned.

literal: On the jiachen day of the sixth month Shenwu returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the sixth month Gao Huan returned to Jinyang.

literal: In the ninth month Shenwu marched west.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Gao Huan marched west.

literal: On the jihai day of the tenth month he besieged Western Wei Yitong Third Rank Wang Sizheng at Yubi city, intending to draw the enemy out; the Western army did not dare emerge.
idiomatic: On the jihai day of the tenth month he besieged Western Wei Wang Sizheng at Yubi, hoping to draw the enemy out; the Western army did not dare sally.

literal: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month Shenwu, because heavy snow had killed many soldiers, thereupon withdrew the army.
idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month heavy snow had killed many soldiers, and Gao Huan withdrew.

literal: On the renshen day of the second month of the first year of Wuding, Beiyu Province Governor Gao Shen held Wulao and rebelled westward.
idiomatic: On the renshen day of the second month of Wuding 1 (543), Governor of Beiyu Gao Shen held Wulao and defected to the west.

literal: On the renchen day of the third month Yuwen Tai led his host to aid Gao Shen and besieged the south city of Heqiao.
idiomatic: On the renchen day of the third month Yuwen Tai marched to aid Gao Shen and besieged the south city of Heqiao.

literal: On the wushen day Shenwu routed them greatly at Mangshan, capturing more than four hundred Western Wei commanders and generals and below, and killing or capturing on the order of sixty thousand.
idiomatic: On the wushen day Gao Huan routed them at Mangshan, taking more than four hundred Western Wei officers and killing or capturing some sixty thousand men.

literal: At that time a soldier stole and killed a donkey; by army law he should die; Shenwu did not kill him but was about to take him to Bing Province for judgment.
idiomatic: A soldier had stolen and killed a donkey—a capital offense by army law; Gao Huan spared him for the moment and meant to judge him at Bing Province.

literal: The next day battle was joined again; he fled to the Western army and reported where Shenwu was.
idiomatic: The next day, when battle resumed, the man fled to the Western army and revealed Gao Huan's position.

literal: The Western army attacked with all its edge; the host collapsed; Shenwu lost his horse; Helian Yangshun dismounted and gave his horse to Shenwu; with the servant Feng Wenluo supporting him they mounted and fled together — followers on foot and horse numbered six or seven.
idiomatic: The Western army struck with its full strength; Gao Huan's force broke; he lost his horse; Helian Yangshun dismounted and gave him his mount; the servant Feng Wenluo helped him up and they fled together with only six or seven followers.

literal: When pursuing horsemen arrived, trusted commander Wei Xingqing said: "My lord, go on; Xingqing has a hundred arrows at his belt — enough to kill a hundred men.
idiomatic: When pursuers closed in, his trusted commander Wei Xingqing said, "My lord, go; I have a hundred arrows at my belt—enough to kill a hundred men.

literal: " Shenwu urged him on, saying: "If the affair succeeds, I will make you Governor of Huaizhou; if you die, I will employ your son.
idiomatic: Gao Huan urged him on, saying, "If we survive, I will make you Governor of Huaizhou; if you die, I will employ your son.

literal: " Xingqing said: "My son is small; I wish you would employ my elder brother.
idiomatic: Xingqing said, "My son is still small; employ my elder brother instead.

literal: " He permitted it.
idiomatic: Gao Huan agreed.

literal: Xingqing fought; when his arrows were exhausted he died.
idiomatic: Xingqing fought until his arrows were spent and died.

literal: Western Wei Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng pursued Shenwu with thirteen horsemen; Hezhou Governor Liu Honghui shot down two of them.
idiomatic: Western Wei Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng pursued Gao Huan with thirteen horsemen; Governor of Hezhou Liu Honghui shot down two.

literal: Sheng's spear was about to strike Shenwu when Duan Xiaoxian shot sideways and killed Sheng's horse; he thus escaped.
idiomatic: Sheng's spear was about to find Gao Huan when Duan Xiaoxian shot across and killed Sheng's horse; Gao Huan escaped.

literal: Yu and Luo — two provinces — were pacified.
idiomatic: Yu and Luo provinces were pacified.

literal: Shenwu sent Liu Feng in pursuit of the fleeing enemy, extended territory to Hongnong, and returned.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Liu Feng in pursuit, extended the frontier to Hongnong, and returned.
